$comment: The commercial catalogue as data. Plans are never hard-coded into a service
or a component (docs/domain-model.md section 4); this file is what a fresh
deployment starts from, and everything after that is edited through the API.
A feature's slug is the slug its package declares. There is no mapping table
between what is sold and what is delivered, because the moment there is one,
the two drift and an entitlement points at nothing
(docs/adr/0029-one-slug-for-the-catalogue-and-the-package.md).
`publish: false` seeds the identity in Draft: it appears in the catalogue and
in the roadmap, and it cannot be sold. That is the honest state for a feature
whose package does not exist yet - the alternative is selling a capability
nothing can deliver. Publishing one is a deliberate act once its package is
in the registry (docs/feature-catalog.md).
Seeding is additive and never deletes. A deployment that was seeded from an
earlier version of this file keeps the identities it already has; retiring
one is a withdrawal through the API, not an edit here.
An operator may point at a different file with Catalogue:SeedPath.
The base store. Present on every store on every plan, never entitled and
never sold. A capability is base if a store cannot function commercially
without it (docs/adr/0024-base-store-versus-optional-feature.md).
features.name: Storefront
features.description: The customer-facing shop: browsing, product pages, cart and the checkout journey.

features.name: Catalogue
features.description: Products or menu items, categories, variants, modifiers, prices and availability.

features.name: Shopper accounts
features.description: Shopper identity, sign-in, guest checkout and the address book.

features.name: Orders and checkout
features.description: The transaction itself: cart totals, checkout, the order lifecycle, cancellation and refund state.

features.name: Payments
features.description: Recording that money arrived, against a provider abstraction. Provider integrations are separate from recording.

$comment: Base as of the catalogue revision: a store must be able to say how it
hands goods over, and zone pricing is part of saying it. Absorbs the
delivery-zones Feature in phase 12.
features.name: Shipping and fulfilment
features.description: Delivery and collection modes, shipping methods, delivery zones and their fees, and fulfilment status.

$comment: Base as of the catalogue revision. Plain coupons are table stakes for a
small store; the sophistication is what is sold, as advanced-promotions.
features.name: Coupons and discounts
features.description: Coupon codes, percentage and fixed discounts, validity periods, minimum order value and product restrictions.

$comment: Optional features, in the order docs/feature-catalog.md develops them.
The four with a package in features/ are published; the rest are Draft
identities so the catalogue and the roadmap are the same list.
features.name: Analytics Core
features.description: Revenue, orders, average order value and best sellers over a date range. The event store everything else analytical builds on.

features.name: Analytics Reports
features.description: A reporting surface over the analytics event stream: daily summaries and exportable figures.

features.name: Log shipping
features.description: The store streams its structured logs to KNIGHT, where they are searchable and retained.

features.name: Advanced Promotions
features.description: Buy X get Y, bundles, category and customer-specific campaigns, scheduling, and stacking rules.

features.name: Reviews and Ratings
features.description: Product reviews, star ratings, verified-purchase badges, merchant replies and moderation.

features.name: Advanced Search
features.description: Full-text search with typo tolerance, filters, facets, sorting and suggestions over the catalogue.

features.name: Loyalty and Rewards
features.description: Points, tiers, earning and redemption rules, and a loyalty ledger per shopper.

features.name: Customer Segmentation
features.description: VIP, new, dormant and high-value segments, recalculated on a schedule from order history.

features.name: Gift Cards and Store Credit
features.description: Gift cards a shopper can buy, send and redeem, and store credit spendable across orders. Carries a financial ledger.

features.name: Marketing Automation
features.description: Abandoned-cart, welcome, post-purchase and win-back campaigns against customer segments.

$comment: The one capability that cannot share a host: it runs model inference on
its own workers, and its cost per customer is not something a shared
machine can bound. Whether a feature needs dedicated infrastructure is
fixed at publication and the aggregate refuses to change it afterwards,
so it is set correctly here or not at all.
features.name: AI Reports
features.description: Automated interpretation of the analytics data: what moved, what is unusual, and what to do about it.

features.name: Advanced Inventory
features.description: Stock movements, reservations, warehouses, low-stock alerts, purchase orders and suppliers.

features.name: Restaurant Operations
features.description: Tables, kitchen order states and display workflow, preparation times, throttling and pickup scheduling.

features.name: Multi-Location
features.description: One merchant, several branches or warehouses: inventory, menus, staff and orders scoped per location.

features.name: Subscriptions and Recurring Orders
features.description: Recurring orders on a schedule, with pause, resume, cancellation and failed-payment handling.

features.name: Marketplace and Delivery Integrations
features.description: Product, order, status and inventory synchronisation with delivery marketplaces, POS and accounting systems.

$comment: Basic is the whole base store and nothing else. It is a working shop, not
a crippled one: the reason to leave it is that KNIGHT helps the merchant
sell more, not that KNIGHT withheld the ability to sell at all.
plans.name: Basic
plans.description: A working store: catalogue, orders, payments, shipping and coupons, on shared hosting.

$comment: Custom is a-la-carte: the base store, plus whichever optional features the
customer switches on for themselves.
Only published features are listed. A Draft feature cannot be entitled
(Feature.CanBeEntitled), so listing one here would put a toggle on the
screen that refuses every time it is used - a screen that looks broken
rather than one that says the capability is not built yet. Each feature
joins its plans in the release that publishes it; seeding is additive, so
adding the line here is all it takes.
plans.name: Custom
plans.description: Basic plus the optional capabilities the customer chooses, one by one.

$comment: Professional is every capability KNIGHT sells, plus a machine of their
own. As with Custom, only published features are listed, so this list
grows with each release rather than promising what is not built. When
ai-reports ships it joins as toggleable rather than included: it is the
one capability with a real per-use cost behind it, and it needs dedicated
infrastructure, which is what this plan provides.
plans.name: Professional
plans.description: Every capability KNIGHT sells, on dedicated infrastructure.

$comment: A bundle is a plan composition, not a package. Bundling is a commercial
act - the same Features at a price that suits a shape of business - and
the moment it becomes a fifteenth package there are two things to build,
test and deliver for one thing to sell.
Only published Features appear, like every other plan. Growth is what it
says today; marketing-automation joins it in phase 15.
plans.name: Growth
plans.description: The base store plus everything that helps a shop sell more: analytics, advanced merchandising, reviews and segments.

$comment: The other half of the same argument. Retention sells the Features a shop
uses on the customers it already has, where Growth sells the ones it uses
to find more.
customer-segmentation is in both, deliberately: it is the Feature that
makes the others worth having, and a bundle that left it out would be
cheaper and worse.
plans.name: Retention
plans.description: The base store plus everything that brings a customer back: loyalty, gift cards, segments and the analytics under them.
